title: Security Is a Practice — Light, Layers, and Honest Claims

intelligence.essence: NayaNET's security is not a wall or a department; it is how the system is built and how the people in it live: everything travels inside one front door, with an ID, on a ledger, with Nayas watching live — and modular construction means one breach never gets everything. This essence carries the practice around the law (the law itself, SN-1855 "Security Is Light," stands alone and is cited, never restated): its ratification and rollout plan, the Secure Network design that makes it concrete, and the official build order — with the honesty caveats at full strength: at filing, mail privacy proof was still owed, the ledger had been frozen since 2026-10-22 in the last live read, and live watch was law, not yet proven 24/7. Citizen-facing claims come only after proof, never before it.
intelligence.human_view: Most systems promise safety. This one describes it: what is protected first, which layers do the protecting, what is still owed, and what nobody is allowed to claim until it's proven. The most important sentences in these notes might be the confessions — a frozen ledger, an unproven watch, a mail door too open — because a security culture that names its holes is the only kind that closes them.
intelligence.child_view: Our village has one gate, and everyone who comes in shows their name tag. Everything anyone does is written in the big book. If one house has a problem, only that house is locked while it's fixed — the whole village doesn't burn. And nobody, not even the mayor, reads anyone else's letters.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's a small town done digitally: one road in, everyone known, everything on the record, and neighbors who actually watch the street. Locks matter, but what keeps a town safe is that nothing happens in the dark. And the town is honest about the one window that still needs a latch.
intelligence.ai_view: Cite SN-1855; never restate it. Before any surface ships, answer its three questions (ledger with identity/scope/value on every action? one block — isolable, provenance-carrying, reversible? friction rising automatically as a verified balance dives?) — any no stops the ship. Gate server-side on every request; log denied attempts as patterns, never content. Name an unseen corner the day you find it. And keep the claim staged: law is not built, built is not proven.
intelligence.what_it_means: Security here is a property of the architecture and the culture together: transparency (the ledger), composition (blocks that isolate damage), and inhabitation (citizens and Nayas as the watch). The practice notes add the fourth property: honesty about the gap between the model and tonight's live state — which is what makes the first three believable.
whats_inside: The law is cited, not paraphrased: SN-1855 stands alone; every surface is scored against its three ship questions before it ships.
Security claims are staged like everything else: what is law, what is built, and what is proven live are three different sentences.
The server denies; the button merely shows. Gating that lives in the interface is cosmetic.
Exceptions are named, singular, and on a cure path — an exception is never a precedent.
Corrections to the record (Smart Meet's tier, the withdrawn figure) are made in the open, in the implementing document itself.
